title: B-tree database page-count header selection

scope.rationale: btreeSetNPage reads the database page count from page-1 header offset 28 and falls back to the Pager page count only when the header field is zero.
excluded_responsibilities: Database-header validation outside the bounded field read

external_source_responsibilities: Pager supplies its current page count to the bounded owner
dependencies.caller_closure: The complete selection helper is integrated into page-1 B-tree locking and the shared page-count owner.

inputs: Shared B-tree, valid page-1 bytes, and current Pager page count
contracts.ownership: Page bytes and shared owner are borrowed; only database_pages is mutated.
contracts.state_and_results: A nonzero big-endian header field wins. Zero selects the Pager count.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Caller owns the B-tree mutex. Pager I/O is outside this bounded representation.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: A page shorter than offset 32 returns Corrupt without updating the count.

representation_differences: Zig receives the already observed Pager count as an explicit u32 argument and reports a bounded short-header error; the source invokes sqlite3PagerPagecount directly.

oracle.protocol: Trace header count zero with Pager count 7, then header count 9 with the same Pager count.
oracle.normalization: Page counts compare as exact unsigned integers.

assurance.io_crash_concurrency: Pager I/O is external; caller owns B-tree synchronization.
assurance.continuation: Short input preserves the prior count; valid input deterministically replaces it.
assurance.performance: Constant-time four-byte decode and one branch.

integration.native_call_path: lockBtree invokes the helper after page-1 header validation; pageCount and lastPage observe the published count.

independent_review.notes: Requires pinned-C page-count trace, assurance closure, and independent review.

known_blockers: Add pinned-C zero/nonzero header differential around Pager fallback.
